habitat: Flocks, from a few birds to hundreds, on shallow inland lakes, dams and pans, especially sewage ponds, and at coastal lagoons and estuaries. It feeds by sweeping the immersed bill from side to side while walking or swimming. It is nomadic when not breeding.
summary: A common resident. Entirely pied, with a thin upturned black bill. The identification line says the legs are white. The description does not repeat the leg colour. Where the adult is black, the immature is dark brown. The call is a liquid kluut. The Kemp name Avocet and the code NB were left unchanged.

similar.note: Black-winged Stilt has a straight bill and very long red legs. Pied Avocet has an upturned bill.

calls.description: A liquid kluut, sometimes from several birds together. Grade A call from Hyères, France, recorded as a chick call. A grade A alarm call from the Eastern Cape ranks lower for a call slot. The filename is XC376940-Cri avocette poussin (2).mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it a common resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. It is nomadic when not breeding. The identification line says the legs are white and the description does not repeat that, so this needs review. The grade A call is a chick call from France. The Eastern Cape grade A file is an alarm call. The Kemp code NB was left unchanged.
